ICICI Bank Nifty 50 weight hits all-time high at 9.45% after three months sprint
ICICI Bank has quietly reached its largest footprint ever in India’s Nifty 50. At the close of September 2, the private sector lender’s weighting in the 50-share Nifty 50 touched an all-time high of 9.45%, as per NSE data.
Thus, overtaking its previous peak of 9.41% logged in July 2025.
The milestone follows a sharp summer run in which ICICI Bank gained 113 basis points of index share in just three months.
After moving sideways between 8.05% and 8.58% across late 2025 and closing May 2026 at 8.32%, the stock steadily outpaced the broader market, climbing to 9.01% in June, 9.22% in July, and topping out at 9.45% in August. Because the Nifty 50 uses free-float market capitalisation, every uptick in the bank’s fully floating share count translates directly into increased index weight.
ICICI Bank’s climb has also shrunk the gap between India's two largest private lenders to its narrowest level since the HDFC twins' mega-merger. With HDFC Bank holding a 9.85% weight at the end of August 2026, ICICI Bank (at 9.45%) now trails the top-weighted banking stock by just 40 basis points. A brief stretch of relative outperformance could see ICICI Bank challenge HDFC Bank for the top banking slot in the Nifty 50.
A five-fold expansion
The bank’s ascent to record weight reflects a multi-year turnaround across two distinct market cycles.
During the aftermath of the Global Financial Crisis in March 2009, ICICI Bank made up a modest 1.96% of the Nifty 50. Since that low, its weight in India's premier equity basket has expanded by nearly 4.8 times.
Even during the Reserve Bank of India’s asset quality review in 2016-2018, when legacy corporate bad loans pulled the bank's index share down to a low of 4.19% in June 2018, the franchise executed a balance sheet cleanup. Over the following eight years, the bank shifted its focus toward retail lending, SME business banking, and technology-driven underwriting, more than doubling its index presence from that trough.
Today, at 9.45%, ICICI Bank sits just 55 basis points away from the 10% mark. Commanding double-digit representation in the Nifty 50 is rare, historically achieved only by names such as Reliance Industries and HDFC Bank.
Why the Street Stays Bullish
The stock maintains a unanimous buy consensus among 42 tracked brokerage analysts. Price targets among foreign brokerages range between Rs 1,700 and Rs 1,935, underpinned by predictable double-digit earnings growth and steady return ratios.
Goldman Sachs (Target: Rs 1,935): Goldman Sachs sees ICICI Bank as a core compounder in Indian banking, pointing to consistent Return on Assets (ROA) above 2.2%. The brokerage expects pre-provision operating profits across the private banking sector to rise at a mid-to-high teens pace through FY27–FY29, with ICICI Bank positioned to gain market share without taking on incremental credit risk.
Bernstein SocGen (Target: Rs 1,800): Bernstein raised its target following robust quarterly performance, highlighting that the bank’s gross non-performing asset (GNPA) profile has stayed benign at around 1.9%. The brokerage noted that the bank's core margin trajectory remains protected as deposit repricing stabilizes, while its low level of unsecured stress provides clear earnings visibility.
Jefferies (Target: Rs 1,750): Retaining ICICI Bank as its top sector pick, Jefferies values the standalone bank at 2.3 times its forward book value (adj. P/BV). The brokerage forecasts loan growth compounding at 15% annually through FY29, supported by manageable credit costs in the 40–50 basis point range and Return on Equity (ROE) hovering near 17%.
JPMorgan and Nomura (Targets: Rs 1,735 and Rs 1,700): Both desks maintain positive stances, highlighting the bank's liability franchise and digital adoption via its iMobile platform. They note that the stock trades around 16 to 18 times forward price-to-earnings (P/E), a reasonable valuation given its sector-leading risk-adjusted returns.
The Passive Flow Advantage
Beyond market prestige, the record 9.45% weighting carries practical implications for capital flows.
With domestic passive investing continuing to expand (through Nifty 50 exchange-traded funds, mutual fund index schemes, and mandatory equity contributions from the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation), capital is deployed strictly in proportion to index weights.
At a 9.45% allocation, nearly Rs 9.45 of every Rs 100 entering Nifty 50-linked passive products is automatically deployed into ICICI Bank shares. This steady institutional inflow creates a structural liquidity cushion, reinforcing the bank's market footprint as it approaches the double-digit threshold.

articles.title: IMD issues red alert in Delhi for heavy rain; Noida, Ghaziabad also experience downpour | India News - Hindustan Times

articles.full_text:
Delhi and its adjoining areas experienced moderate to heavy rain from afternoon on Friday, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to elevate the yellow warning for the city to a red alert, cautioning of more downpour accompanied with thunderstorms.
While the weather conditions impacted flight operations in Delhi, the Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport was also left heavily waterlogged on Friday after several hours of rain. Visuals from the airport showed people carrying luggage trolleys through ankle-deep water.
Nine flights — four to Jaipur, as many to Lucknow and one to Ahmedabad — were diverted between 3:30 pm and 4:30 pm.
Air India issued an advisory for its passengers and said in a post on X that flight operations to and from Delhi stand chances of being affected due to adverse weather conditions.
Along with Delhi, Uttar Pradesh's Noida and Ghaziabad were also placed under an orange warning by the IMD, according to the nowcast seen on its website at around 3:30 pm. There was no warning for Haryana's Gurugram.
According to the IMD's three-hourly rainfall data cited in a PTI news agency report, Palam recorded 3.4 mm of rain between 11.30 am and 2.30 pm, while Najafgarh received 0.5 mm between 8.30 am and 11.30 am. Most other monitoring stations recorded no rainfall during these periods.
Some parts of Delhi and its adjoining areas also experienced severe waterlogging after hours-long rain, with vehicles seen wading through flooded streets in videos.
Delhi temperature
Delhi on Friday recorded minimum temperature at 25.5 degrees Celsius, 0.1 degrees above normal, according to station-wise data from Palam, while Lodhi Road recorded 27.6 degrees Celsius, 2.6 degrees above normal.
The Ridge recorded a minimum of 23.7 degrees Celsius, 0.5 degrees below normal, while Ayanagar recorded 27 degrees Celsius, 2.3 degrees above normal.
The maximum temperature was expected to hover around 32 degrees Celsius, while humidity was recorded at 75 per cent in the morning hours.
Wetter-than-normal August
The latest spell comes after a wetter-than-normal August for the capital. Delhi recorded 354.1 mm of rainfall between August 1 and August 30 till 5:30pm, more than 120mm above the IMD’s long-period average (LPA) of 233.1 mm for the month, HT earlier reported.
The city had also logged excess August rainfall in 2025 and 2024, when it received 400.81mm and 390.3mm, respectively. These were the first instances since 2020 when August rainfall crossed the LPA, with the city recording 237 mm that year.
Since 2011, Delhi has crossed the August rainfall LPA only six times — in 2012, 2013, 2020, 2024, 2025 and 2026.
Meanwhile, Haryana recorded its first rainfall deficit for August in three years, receiving 138.5 mm of rain against the normal 146.1 mm, a shortfall of 5%, according to IMD data.
Gurugram recorded 217.4 mm of rainfall against a normal of 185.1 mm, a surplus of 17%, placing the district in the normal rainfall category, as per IMD. The city received 66.5 mm of rainfall between August 21 and 27, which was 58% above its normal weekly rainfall.

2 Filipino seafarers killed in Strait of Hormuz as Philippines maintains red alert
- PUBLISHED: Fri 4 Sept 2026, 10:32 AM
[Editor's Note: For the latest updates on the US-Iran conflict, follow the Khaleej Times live blog.]
The Philippine Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) announced the Strait of Hormuz shall remain on red alert status for the world’s biggest supplier of maritime labour following the deaths of two Filipino seafarers on Monday.
DMW secretary Hans Leo Cacdac said the narrow passageway to and from the Arabian Gulf is still considered a “high-risk, war-like zone,” reminding shipowners to avoid sending Filipino seafarers through the area “when possible.”
“Shipowners must comply with safety requirements before allowing Filipino seafarers to undertake voyages through high-risk waters,” Cacdac said. The requirements include risk assessments, security protocols, possible ship escorts, armed guards and reporting mechanisms, the official said.
Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels.
Cacdac reminded Filipino seafarers they have a right to refuse to sail through the dangerous route, pointing out that 31 ships carrying 421 Filipino seafarers have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz since the start of the hostilities in the area on February 28.
Of these, 406 Filipino seafarers were unharmed, 10 were injured but have recovered, three died and one remains officially missing. About 268 have already returned to the Philippines.
More deaths
The latest victims were serving as crew members of crude oil tanker Sidr when it was struck by “unidentified projectiles” while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Sidr is owned by Bahri, the national shipping company of Saudi Arabia.
While Bahri maintains the safety and well-being of its people remain its “highest priority” and it is committed to operating according to the “highest standards of safety and security,” the company said in a statement. However, it has yet to disclose the reasons why its ship transited the dangerous waterway amid renewed hostilities between the US and Iran.
Bahri said it was deeply saddened by the loss of two Filipino seafarers and extended its condolences to their families, loved ones and colleagues. It also assured its full support to the affected families and crew and remained in contact with the vessel.
Scrambling for support
Monday’s attack is forcing the Philippine government to step up efforts to repatriate affected seafarers in the region, including the 14 surviving Filipino seafarers.
Cacdac said the government is yet to bring home the remains of the two fatalities and provide support to their families.
The remains of the fatalities have been offloaded in Oman, the Philippine government announced. Philippine Labor Attaché Alice Visperas has been dispatched to the Middle Eastern Sultanate to personally oversee the repatriation of the remains.
On Thursday, Cacdac visited one of the victims’ families in Laguna Province to extend official condolences. He praised his compatriot sailors for helping contain the fires aboard the ship after the attack.
The Philippines supplies up to 550,000 active seafarers globally, making it the world's leading source of maritime labor. Filipino mariners make up roughly 30 per cent of the entire global seafaring workforce.
The country’s government, highly dependent on remittances by overseas Filipinos, keeps sending workers abroad to keep its economy afloat. Amid increasing attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Black Sea, the country could only remind employers and employees about safety protocols, remotely hoping for compliance and positive results.
